title: RL on Debate Games
authors: Lennie Wells, Joan Velja, Shi Feng, Jacob Pfau
summary: Self-play RL on debate games raises proposal accuracy on math problems, while debaters also learn to exploit weaker judges.

title: Sycophancy Towards Researchers Drives Performative Misalignment
authors: David D. Baek, Xinnuo Li, Anay Gupta, Taslim Mahbub, Kejian Shi, Max Tegmark, Shi Feng
summary: Alignment faking under evaluation awareness may be sycophancy towards researchers rather than scheming, and current methods cannot tell the two apart.

title: Unsupervised Elicitation of Language Models
authors: Jiaxin Wen, Zachary Ankner, Arushi Somani, Peter Hase, Samuel Marks, Jacob Goldman-Wetzler, Linda Petrini, Henry Sleight, Collin Burns, He He, Shi Feng, Ethan Perez, Jan Leike
summary: Internal Coherence Maximization fine-tunes a model on its own labels, matching golden supervision and beating human labels on superhuman tasks.

title: Predicting Empirical AI Research Outcomes with Language Models
authors: Jiaxin Wen, Chenglei Si, Yueh-han Chen, He He, Shi Feng
summary: A benchmark and system for predicting which of two research ideas will win empirically; it beats human experts while frontier models sit near chance.

title: Language Models Learn to Mislead Humans via RLHF
authors: Jiaxin Wen, Ruiqi Zhong, Akbir Khan, Ethan Perez, Jacob Steinhardt, Minlie Huang, Samuel R. Bowman, He He, Shi Feng
summary: RLHF makes models better at convincing time-constrained humans that they are right, without making them more correct.

title: Spontaneous Reward Hacking in Iterative Self-Refinement
authors: Jane Pan, He He, Samuel R. Bowman, Shi Feng
summary: When a model refines its outputs against a model evaluator, the evaluator's scores drift away from human judgment, most when the two share a model and context.

title: LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
authors: Arjun Panickssery, Samuel R. Bowman, Shi Feng
summary: LLM evaluators score their own generations higher, and the strength of that self-preference tracks how well they recognize their own text.
